name: Mijamin
overview: Mijamin was a male Levite who served as the sixth-chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses established in Israel. He belonged to the line of Ithamar, one of the two sons of Aaron through whom the priestly divisions were organized. His role as a priest highlights his importance in the religious life of Israel during the time of the divided priestly courses.
namesAndTitles: The name Mijamin means 'from the right hand,' which may imply a position of favor or strength. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:9 and was not given directly by God but reflects a meaningful Hebrew designation within the priestly lineage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Mijamin as a descendant of Ithamar, linking him to the priestly line stemming from Aaron's son. Beyond this lineage, no additional family relationships are recorded for Mijamin in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mijamin's significance lies in his role as one of the twenty-four priestly courses established to organize the service of the priests in the temple. Being the sixth course chosen, he represents the continuation of the priestly duties through Ithamar's lineage, emphasizing the structured and divinely ordained worship system in Israel. His inclusion in 1 Chronicles 24 underscores the detailed care God took in arranging the priesthood for orderly worship.
